- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true values show a clear downward trend or mean reversion.
- Model often fails to adjust for recent downward momentum — if the last 5–7 days show falling prices, forecast still holds or even rises.
- Model tends to ignore or underweight the influence of recent low prices (e.g., 50–60 range) when forecasting, leading to overestimation of future values.
- Model shows lag in reacting to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a sharp decline.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike after minor price movements, then fail to correct.
- Model underestimates the impact of seasonal or policy-driven downward pressure (e.g., ETS auction cycles, regulatory changes) — especially in the final 10–15 days.
